text: Farmers can produce their own protein-rich feed supplements. Maggots: insect larvae raised on kitchen and vegetable waste decomposing in a tank (adding poultry droppings can boost production); the tank should be covered during the hottest hours to protect eggs, and larvae develop in 5–10 days before being collected as feed. Earthworms: raised on a substrate of cow manure, corn stalks, and fresh leaves mixed with water, covered with plastic and left to ferment for 2 weeks in a shaded, regularly watered container; worms are harvested after about 1 month. Termites: chopped straw mixed with cattle manure is moistened, placed in clay pots, and the pot's mouth is set over a hole in an active termite colony; after 3–4 weeks a new colony should establish inside the container, and its eggs and larvae are fed to chickens.
